A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TBIK research and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices. Material can be matched across the substantial reorganization, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D report original reproducibility measurements, kernel and end-to-end performance results, and vLLM–FSDP probability-gap experiments.

after.justification: The retained empirical evaluations are supplemented by original GSM8K reinforcement-learning results and revised latency experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes from all-gather followed by local pairwise summation in v1 to distributed tree reduction followed by broadcast in v2. This revises the communication procedure while retaining the MatMul algorithm and fixed global binary-tree accumulation order.

E1.justification: V2 adds GSM8K for actual online GRPO training and policy evaluation. This substantially extends empirical task coverage beyond v1's AIME24/AMC23 inference reproducibility and fixed-response training–inference mismatch measurements.

E2.justification: The main BF16, BIO, and cuBLAS comparisons remain. V2 adds BIO as an explicit reference in the component latency comparison and removes the standalone measured NCCL all-reduce comparison from v1 Figure 11. Newly discussed FP16, SIS, TIS, and GSPO approaches are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Latency evaluation changes from vLLM on four L40S GPUs without NVLink to SGLang on four H20 GPUs with NVLink. V2 also introduces a GRPO protocol using Qwen3-1.7B, 256 training and 64 evaluation questions, and entropy, KL divergence, reward, and Pass@1 measurements. The original reproducibility configuration grid remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablation is revised: v1 Appendix D tests MatMul, all-reduce, and their combination without BIO; v2 Appendix H includes BIO alone and tests each component on that common base. The standalone all-reduce latency-versus-size analysis is removed. These are bounded changes to the existing overhead analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify inference seed 42 and retain the same accuracy standard-deviation analysis across TP configurations. V2 adds no repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or identified uncertainty-estimation procedure for its RL results.

E6.justification: V2 adds RL learning curves showing zero rollout–training KL divergence and Pass@1 reaching approximately 0.73 with BIO+TBIK. Latency results are replaced, reporting 22–63% total overhead versus v1's 56–135% under different hardware/software settings; this is not a same-setting speedup. All four matched reproducibility tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix C adds T(k1)=k1 for t=0 to the recursive reduction definition, completing a missing singleton boundary case. The theorem and induction argument otherwise match v1 Section 4.3; moving the proof does not constitute additional theoretical content.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes bitwise determinism and providing a foundation for on-policy RL. V2's abstract and conclusion additionally claim true on-policy RL at scale for the first time, faster convergence, and improved model performance, substantially extending the claimed contribution to training outcomes.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its RL curves as evidence that eliminating numerical mismatch improves convergence and policy performance. Its overhead discussion changes with the NVLink setting, emphasizing implementation costs rather than the earlier communication bottleneck. It also drops v1's explicit deterministic-communication qualification for pipeline-parallel determinism.

D1.justification: Appendix I.2 adds an RL recipe, including group size 8, rollout/training batch sizes 64/32, a 512-token limit, and learning rate 1e-5. V2 omits v1's project code link and the four-prompt AIME probability-gap procedure. Existing decoding parameters and block-size settings are retained through relocation.

R1.justification: New Appendix A expands positioning beyond batch-invariant kernels to FP16, sequence-level importance sampling, truncated importance sampling, and GSPO. It distinguishes their partial mismatch mitigation from TBIK's claimed bitwise on-policy guarantee, accompanying the new priority claim and additional RL and evaluation references.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses the introduction, merges the BIO and parallelism discussions, rewrites the kernel-design section, and moves the proof and detailed implementation material into reorganized appendices. It also adds related-work and impact sections and revises the abstract and conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the motivating schematic, splits the kernel-throughput plot into BF16/FP32 panels, adds a four-panel RL figure, and redesigns the component comparison with five configurations. Several diagrams move to appendices; v1's preliminary unique-output table and standalone all-reduce plot disappear. These exceed simple renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The GSM8K learning curves provide actual RL-training evidence missing from v1, while the BIO-controlled component analysis and corrected recursive definition improve support and clarity. The gain remains limited by the small 256/64-question study without reported training uncertainty, stronger at-scale claims, and loss of the code pointer and some probability-gap protocol details.
